context_blocks.text: # 6\. Squirrel Influences: Elevated Anchors, Redundant Routes, and Scatter Topology

context_blocks.parent_heading: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
context_blocks.text: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT

target_blocks.text: | Tree hollows and dreys     | Primary refuge, nursery drey, guest drey, seasonal and emergency nodes. |
| Branch and trunk movement  | Bridges, runs, trunk arterials, lookout crowns, meeting branches.   |
| Scatter-hoarding           | Named cache points, route stores, emergency reserves, remembered ownership. |
| Canopy gap response        | Route engineering, landing platforms, intermediate perches, wind braces. |
| Human structures as canopy | Sign towers, cable roads, pipe perches, wall seams, girder routes.  |

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
target_blocks.text:
<!--@9¶1-->
The placement verbs should remain cultural instructions rather than zoological reflexes. Ecology provides the reason each culture finds its verb emotionally and physically satisfying.

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
# 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
target_blocks.text: | Mouse       | JOIN                 | Edge contact, enclosure, dense micro-habitat.         |

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
target_blocks.text: | Rabbit      | GATHER               | Shared surface life held close to concealment.        |

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
target_blocks.text: | Squirrel    | CONNECT              | Vertical anchors, gap trajectories, multiple refuges. |

target_blocks.parent_heading: # 7\. Ecological Foundations of JOIN, GATHER, and CONNECT
target_blocks.text:
VISIBLE SAFETY TRIAD
Mouse is enclosed. Rabbit is concealed. Squirrel is elevated.
| ROOM -\> WING -\> CONNECTED SECOND HOUSE  | COMPLETE COURT -\> BUD DAUGHTER COURT -\> CONNECT                | REACH -\> REINFORCE -\> THICKEN INTO LOOPS                                         |
| Expansion thickens an inhabited envelope. | Expansion creates another social center inside protective cover. | Expansion establishes distance, then turns a fragile strand into a resilient mesh. |

<!--@10¶1-->
A single roadside object should support different readings depending on species scale and body. This is one of the most valuable environmental-design consequences of the ecology work: the map does not need three separate biomes to support three distinct civilizations.
